name: ProdMan.AI outside resources
method: Each resource scored 1 to 5 on seven criteria with fixed weights; weighted_score = sum(weight x score / 5). Quality of output comes from the round 3 blind research benchmark where a resource was tested; otherwise it is null and the total uses the plain Claude baseline (4). Three pass or fail checks come first: licence read at source, privacy and security, and a commit in the last 180 days (or a vendor documenting a hosted service as current).

transparency_licence_and_cost.why: Data handling stated plainly; closed hosted service.

maintenance_and_reliability.why: Vendor documents it as current; service accounts still in beta.

resources.name: PostHog MCP server
resources.licence: MIT for the server code (services/mcp sits outside the ee/ folder); hosted at mcp.posthog.com under PostHog's terms
resources.licence_evidence: PostHog/posthog LICENSE: content outside ee/ is under the MIT Expat licence; services/mcp/package.json declares MIT.
resources.install: npx @posthog/wizard@latest mcp add (PostHog's installer), or add https://mcp.posthog.com/mcp by hand with a personal API key

executes_code.what: The installer runs an npm package on your machine (@posthog/wizard); the manual route runs mcp-remote through npx.

sends_data.where: PostHog data moves between PostHog and Claude. Connecting is free, but some tools use LLMs inside PostHog and may be billed as PostHog AI spend; those need AI data processing switched on. Tools can create feature flags and experiments.

real_world_pm_usefulness.why: Analytics and SQL, dashboards, experiments, feature flags, surveys, replays and error tracking.

quality_of_output.why: Not benchmarked. For the total only, the plain Claude baseline (4 of 5, round 3) is used, because there is no evidence it does better or worse than Claude alone.

ease_of_setup_and_usability.why: Needs Node and an installer, or a personal API key.

integration_with_claude.why: Installer supports Claude Code; not in Anthropic's PM plugin connector list.

reusability_across_workflows.why: Feeds metrics reviews, experiment readouts and incident checks.

transparency_licence_and_cost.why: MIT code you can read; some tools add PostHog AI spend.

resources.prerequisites: Claude Code, Python 3 for the review app, and your AI feature's outputs or traces as JSONL, CSV or JSON.

executes_code.what: error-discovery has Claude build an HTML review app and serve it with a local Python standard library server. The npx route runs the skills command line tool.

sends_data.where: Reads your trace files locally; nothing beyond your Claude session.

real_world_pm_usefulness.why: The method PMs need before shipping an AI feature, but only for AI features.

quality_of_output.why: Not benchmarked. For the total only, the plain Claude baseline (4 of 5, round 3) is used, because there is no evidence it does better or worse than Claude alone.

ease_of_setup_and_usability.why: One documented npx command, or two plugin commands; needs real traces and Python for the review app.

integration_with_claude.why: Claude Code plugin and npx skills; no Claude app route documented.

reusability_across_workflows.why: One job, evals, used in every AI feature cycle.

transparency_licence_and_cost.why: Apache 2.0 and free; the course is a separate paid offer.

resources.name: Figma MCP server and plugin
resources.last_commit: 2026-10-05 (guide repository). The server is hosted by Figma.
resources.licence: No licence file; use is under the Figma Developer Terms
resources.licence_evidence: The repository has no LICENSE file (GitHub API 404). README: by using the server and its skills you agree to the Figma Developer Terms; the skills are a beta feature. The Developer Terms (last updated 5 May 2026, read 2026-10-11) grant a limited licence to use Figma's developer resources to develop, test and support an integration or connection with Figma as its developer documentation permits; the documented plugin is such a connection.
resources.install: claude plugin install figma@claude-plugins-official (or claude mcp add --transport http figma https://mcp.figma.com/mcp)
resources.prerequisites: A Figma account. The Starter plan and View or Collab seats get up to 6 tool calls a month; Dev or Full seats on paid plans get per minute limits.

executes_code.what: Runs at Figma; the listed skills are markdown.

sends_data.where: Design files you open move between Figma and Claude. Writing to the canvas is free during the beta and will become a usage based paid feature; generate_image spends Figma AI credits after asking you.

real_world_pm_usefulness.why: Reads design context, draws FigJam diagrams and turns a PRD into a project plan board, but a PM on a View or Collab seat, or on the Starter plan, gets 6 tool calls a month.

quality_of_output.why: Not benchmarked. For the total only, the plain Claude baseline (4 of 5, round 3) is used, because there is no evidence it does better or worse than Claude alone.

ease_of_setup_and_usability.why: One command, then seat and plan limits decide how much you get.

integration_with_claude.why: Official plugin in Anthropic's claude-plugins-official marketplace.

reusability_across_workflows.why: Mostly design and design to code; FigJam boards help planning.

transparency_licence_and_cost.why: No open licence; canvas writing will be paid; image generation uses credits.
